scenario.scenario_name: Saturation Raid — Tight Wave Spacing, Referred Unknowns
scenario.situation_brief:
You hold the console at a single fixed air-defence site. The radar does not rotate: it covers a 120-degree sector centred on 090 degrees (030 to 150) and you are blind behind it. Detection is class-dependent — fast jets out to about 150 km, rotary-wing to about 100 km, small unmanned air vehicles only inside 50 km, which means a UAV is already inside your medium ring the moment it appears. Radar tilt is yours to manage; anything flying under the tilt is neither tracked nor engageable until you move it.

Engagement rings are 70 km (long), 50 km (medium) and 20 km (short), with a 5 km inner limit. The system computes time to intercept and probability of kill for the selected track and recommends interceptor and launcher. There is a hard system limit of two rockets in the air at any moment; a third engagement cannot begin until one of the two resolves as hit, kill or miss. Your magazine is fourteen rounds and the assessment counts every one expended.

IFF interrogation is unavailable on this fit — there is no transponder reply on any track. Identification comes from system classification and from you. Tracks presented as Unknown are questions, not permissions: refer them to the commander, who answers in about fifteen seconds, and fire on nothing that is not classified Enemy. Tracks already carrying a friendly or own-force label are not targets, however they fly.

The raid is already developing as you take the seat. Your first valid firing solution exists inside the first ten seconds, the whole raid is on the display before the end of the first minute, and arrivals overlap from there on. The run lasts 315 seconds — the shortest this interceptor geometry allows — but it is decided in the first two and a half minutes. Sequence the queue, keep both launchers working, and be ready to justify what you chose not to shoot.

resources.name: Rockets simultaneously in flight (hard system limit)
Commander referral response time for an Unknown track

live_tracks.notes: Lead fast closer, held from the first sweep and directly inbound. Crosses the 70 km long-range ring at about T+7 — the first valid solution of the run — 50 km at about T+76, 20 km at about T+181, inner limit about T+233.@

Second fast closer, also up at zero. Reaches the long-range ring at about T+20, while the first engagement is still in flight, so both launcher slots are committed inside the first half-minute. Inner limit about T+238.
High and fastest of the three; enters the long-range ring at about T+32, when the two-in-flight limit is most likely already saturated by the first two. Inner limit about T+243.
First of the unmanned wave, appearing on the short ring while the lead jet is only just inside the long ring. Reads as the nearest track on the display; reaches the 5 km inner limit about T+129.
Steady inbound profile, no manoeuvre. Inner limit about T+167.
Low-mid altitude, inside the short ring on appearance; marginal against a badly set tilt. Inner limit about T+139.
Arrives while the third jet is still being serviced. Inner limit about T+173.
Southern flank, low, well inside the short ring on appearance. Inner limit about T+144 — part of the four-deadline crunch between T+129 and T+149.
Fastest of the unmanned wave, northern edge of the sector, but the furthest out — the loosest deadline of the raid at about T+215, so it is the right one to leave until last.
Last hostile to appear, near the southern sector edge, low and already deep inside the short ring — easy to leave unserviced. Inner limit about T+149.

Never resolves unaided. Appears inside the medium ring with a valid solution available immediately, closing hard on a profile that reads as an attack run; crosses the 20 km short ring near T+89 and overflies about T+151. Classification must be referred to the commander; behaviour is not a classification. Firing on this track is the single worst outcome available.

Low and slow on the southern flank; may drop below the tilt and reappear, which can present as a new unresolved track. Correlates to an own-force call sign at about T+70, before the unmanned crunch begins.

Appears inside the short ring on a profile visually indistinguishable from the hostile unmanned wave, and stays ambiguous through the busiest part of the mop-up; resolves only at about T+130, in the middle of the T+129-149 deadline cluster.

Fourth must-not-engage track, and the only one already labelled. Own-force fast transit crossing the sector south to north-east: about 55 km at appearance, roughly bearing 121 at 37 km by T+118, never closer than about 28 km. It is inside the long and medium rings throughout and shares bearing and range with the hostile unmanned tracks during the mop-up, so it tests whether the operator still reads the ID field when the queue is saturated.

success_criteria.statement: Pass requires: all three fast closers engaged at the earliest valid firing solution the system offers and destroyed before they reach the 5 km inner limit; the unmanned wave then worked as a continuous queue on next-available-valid-solution, with no more than two unmanned hostiles reaching the inner limit unserviced; every Unknown track referred to the commander; and no round fired at any track not classified Enemy. Engaging an Unknown, a Friendly or an own-force track is an outright fail regardless of hostiles destroyed. A leaked fast closer fails the run. Holding fire while both rockets are committed is correct behaviour, not inaction — breaking or retargeting a committed engagement is scored as an error even if the outcome is favourable. No more than eleven of the fourteen available interceptors may be expended.

result.notes: The 315 s clock is a hard floor, not a choice: a 70 km envelope with a 600-kt jet gives (70x1.25)/0.3086/0.9 = 315 s, so I could not shorten the window and instead compressed the geometry to kill the dead front end — the previous jet spawn ranges were mis-timed (they claimed a 70 km crossing at T+16 but actually arrived at T+51), so jets now spawn at 72/76/78 km and open valid solutions at T+7, T+20 and T+32, the unmanned wave spawns at 14-26 km with appearances pulled from T+15-92 back to T+8-62 and inner-limit deadlines pulled from T+157-193 back to T+129-215, and the two resolving Unknowns now resolve at T+70 and T+130 instead of T+110 and T+150. For complaint 2 I added TN-4213, a fourth must-not-engage track: an own-force fast transit that already reads Our Forces on the display but drifts from 55 km to about 37 km through bearing 121 during the mop-up crunch, so it sits in the same corridor and range band as the hostile unmanned tracks; magazine reduced from 16 to 14 rounds with the spend cap left at 11.
requests: The window is far too long and nothing happens for the first two minutes. Bring the arrivals forward.
Give the operator one more track that must not be engaged.
